question: How much revenue do missed calls cost Punctual Pros?
html:
What Missed Calls Cost Punctual Pros

Missed calls cost Punctual Pros an estimated $1.4M a year in recoverable jobs (est.), about 6% of estimated revenue (Voice AI research). This is a conservative model. Actual call logs have not been loaded, so treat it as a sizing range, not a measured figure.

How the estimate is built

  • Call volume: about 3,502 inbound calls a month (est.). This is backed out of the ~$22M revenue estimate, not observed (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Missed share: 14.8% (est.). This blends 12% of calls arriving after hours, with 35% of those lost, and 88% arriving in the day, with 12% missed (Voice AI research).
  • Haircuts: 80% recovered with AI answering, 45% booked, and a 40% cut for callers who would have called back. That leaves about 1,343 incremental jobs at a $1,024 average ticket (Voice AI research).
ComponentAnnual est.
After-hours missed calls$390,000
Daytime and storm overflow$982,000
Recovered from missed calls$1,372,000
Outbound member renewals (separate lever)$403,000
Total voice opportunity$1,775,000 (8.1% of revenue)

Where the estimate is weak

  • The revenue base is soft. FY2025 revenue is ~$22M (range $16-28M), at medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings). Every downstream figure scales with it.
  • The missed share could be much higher. The model tests a range of 10-35%. An industry benchmark finds only 52% of home-services callers reach a person (Voice AI research).
  • Seasonality is missing. Off-hours calls were 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October 2025. Leakage likely clusters in peak months, which a flat annual model understates (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • Benchmarks are unaudited. Booking rates from vendors are self-reported (Voice AI research).
  • The member count is assumed. The 6,000-member figure behind the renewal number is an assumption, not data.

What data would settle it

  • 12 months of ServiceTitan and phone-system logs. These would show answered, abandoned and voicemail calls by hour, trade and territory.
  • Actual booking rate and average ticket by trade.
  • Callback rate on missed numbers. This tests the 40% incrementality haircut.
  • The current membership count and renewal rate.

Next actions

  1. Pull call-detail records and ServiceTitan booking history for the 25 territories. Replace the backed-out call volume and missed share with actuals.
  2. Re-run the model by month and county using the Punctual Pros demand model. This would size peak-season and storm-day leakage.
  3. Pilot AI after-hours answering in one high-volume Pennsylvania territory. Measure booked jobs against a matched control territory.
  4. Confirm the membership count and renewal rate before committing to the outbound renewal lever.
markdown:
# What Missed Calls Cost Punctual Pros

Missed calls cost Punctual Pros an estimated **$1.4M a year** in recoverable jobs (est.), about 6% of estimated revenue (Voice AI research). This is a conservative model. Actual call logs have not been loaded, so treat it as a sizing range, not a measured figure.

## How the estimate is built

- **Call volume:** about 3,502 inbound calls a month (est.). This is backed out of the ~$22M revenue estimate, not observed (Voice AI research; Punctual Pros public filings).
- **Missed share:** 14.8% (est.). This blends 12% of calls arriving after hours, with 35% of those lost, and 88% arriving in the day, with 12% missed (Voice AI research).
- **Haircuts:** 80% recovered with AI answering, 45% booked, and a 40% cut for callers who would have called back. That leaves about 1,343 incremental jobs at a $1,024 average ticket (Voice AI research).

| Component | Annual est. |
|---|---|
| After-hours missed calls | $390,000 |
| Daytime and storm overflow | $982,000 |
| **Recovered from missed calls** | **$1,372,000** |
| Outbound member renewals (separate lever) | $403,000 |
| Total voice opportunity | $1,775,000 (8.1% of revenue) |

## Where the estimate is weak

- **The revenue base is soft.** FY2025 revenue is ~$22M (range $16-28M), at medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings). Every downstream figure scales with it.
- **The missed share could be much higher.** The model tests a range of 10-35%. An industry benchmark finds only 52% of home-services callers reach a person (Voice AI research).
- **Seasonality is missing.** Off-hours calls were 14.1% of HVAC inbound in June versus 9.8% in October 2025. Leakage likely clusters in peak months, which a flat annual model understates (Punctual Pros demand model).
- **Benchmarks are unaudited.** Booking rates from vendors are self-reported (Voice AI research).
- **The member count is assumed.** The 6,000-member figure behind the renewal number is an assumption, not data.

## What data would settle it

- 12 months of ServiceTitan and phone-system logs. These would show answered, abandoned and voicemail calls by hour, trade and territory.
- Actual booking rate and average ticket by trade.
- Callback rate on missed numbers. This tests the 40% incrementality haircut.
- The current membership count and renewal rate.

## Next actions

1. Pull call-detail records and ServiceTitan booking history for the 25 territories. Replace the backed-out call volume and missed share with actuals.
2. Re-run the model by month and county using the Punctual Pros demand model. This would size peak-season and storm-day leakage.
3. Pilot AI after-hours answering in one high-volume Pennsylvania territory. Measure booked jobs against a matched control territory.
4. Confirm the membership count and renewal rate before committing to the outbound renewal lever.
